chemistry.rates-practical-items.0011.all: Handle hot tubes with tongs / wear eye protection / take care not to scald (keep bath stable).

chemistry.rates-recall-facts.0012.a: Particles must collide; with energy at least equal to the activation energy.
chemistry.rates-recall-facts.0012.b: Rate decreases (fastest at the start) as reactants are used up.

chemistry.reactivity-explain-items.0014.all: Aluminium gains oxygen / loses electrons so is oxidised; iron(III) oxide loses oxygen / Fe3+ gains electrons so is reduced; both occur together.

chemistry.reactivity-extended-items.0003.all: Add pieces of each metal to solutions of salts of the other metals (e.g. sulfates) in spotting tile/test tubes; same concentration/volume; observe for coating/colour change/temperature rise; a metal that displaces another is more reactive; count displacements per metal; Mg displaces all, Cu none; place X by which salts it displaces. Safety, fair test.

chemistry.reactivity-mcq-facts.0011.all: attaching blocks of magnesium to a steel hull

chemistry.reactivity-practical-items.001.all: Repeat the experiment and calculate a mean (discard anomalies).

chemistry.reactivity-temp-data.0012.c: All metals are more reactive than silver, so all displace silver; displacement is exothermic.

chemistry.reactivity2-extended-items.000.all: Reacts with acid so above hydrogen; no reaction with cold water so below Ca/Mg; displaces Cu so more reactive than Cu; doesn't displace Zn so less reactive than Zn: X between zinc and copper (e.g. iron/tin/lead region). Further tests: react X with steam; compare rate with acid vs iron/zinc (same conc, size); test whether X displaces iron/lead from their salt solutions; temperature rise in displacement.

chemistry.salts-extended-items.0006.all: Barium sulfate is insoluble so use precipitation: mix solutions of barium chloride (or barium nitrate) and sodium sulfate (or dilute sulfuric acid); stir; precipitate of BaSO4 forms; filter; wash residue with distilled water; dry in a warm oven / between filter papers.

chemistry.salts-practical-items.0008.all: NaOH and H2SO4 are both soluble solutions so excess cannot be removed by filtering; titration (with indicator) finds exact volumes for neutralisation, then repeat without indicator. CuO is an insoluble solid base, so add excess and filter off the unreacted solid.

chemistry.salts-recall-facts.0008.all: A base that is soluble in water (forms OH- ions in solution).

chemistry.states-explain-items.0008.all: Energy supplied is used to overcome the intermolecular forces between water molecules (change of state), not to increase kinetic energy, so temperature does not rise.

chemistry.states-practical-items.0006.all: Record the temperature at which crystals first appear; saturated when the first crystals form.

chemistry.states-recall-facts.0012.all: Particles far apart, randomly arranged; move rapidly in random directions (constant random motion).

chemistry.states-sol-calc.0006.b: mass salt 8.55 g; 8.55/15.54 x 100 = 55.0 g per 100 g water

chemistry.tests-describe-items.0004.all: Add dilute hydrochloric acid; effervescence; bubble gas through limewater which turns milky (CO2).

chemistry.tests-extended-items.0010.all: Flame test with clean nichrome wire dipped in conc HCl: lilac flame = K+. Add dilute HCl to solid: fizzing; gas through limewater turns milky = CO3 2-. Optional: dissolve, NaOH gives no precipitate; no ppt with acidified AgNO3/BaCl2 (rules out halide/sulfate).

chemistry.tests-identify-data.0015.a: Lithium bromide (red flame Li+, cream ppt Br-)
chemistry.tests-identify-data.0015.b: Iron(III) carbonate (brown ppt Fe3+, fizz/limewater CO3 2-) - but this compound is not realistic and would not dissolve in water.
chemistry.tests-identify-data.0015.c: Calcium chloride (orange-red flame Ca2+, white ppt Cl-)

chemistry.states-sol-curve.0007.problem: (b) tolerance 'ALLOW 99 to 100' does not include the computed value 100.9; a correct curve reading of 101 would be rejected.
chemistry.states-sol-curve.0007.fix: (b) 101 g per 100 g water, ALLOW 99 to 103.

chemistry.tests-identify-data.0015.problem: Q is meant to be iron(III) carbonate, which is not a stable real compound and would be insoluble anyway, contradicting 'each solid is dissolved in water first'.
chemistry.tests-identify-data.0015.fix: Make Q iron(II) sulfate (green precipitate with NaOH; white precipitate with BaCl2) or iron(III) chloride, or make Q a Group 1 carbonate with a matching flame test.
